examples.ko: 어제 못 본 드라마를 재방송으로 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the drama I missed yesterday as a re-run.
This program is re-aired on weekends.
The re-run comes on at ten in the morning.
Even just watching the re-run, I can understand the whole story.

examples.ko: 인기 있는 드라마는 재방송도 자주 해요.
examples.en: Popular dramas are re-aired often too.

examples.ko: 저는 재방송에서 처음 그 가수를 봤어요.
examples.en: I first saw that singer in a re-run.

explain: 처음 방송하는 것은 '본방송', 줄여서 '본방'이라고 해요. 본방을 놓친 드라마는 재방송으로 보면 돼요.
explain_en: The first airing is called 본방송, shortened to 본방. If you miss a drama on its first airing, you can watch the 재방송 instead.

examples.ko: 홈페이지 방문자가 하루에 천 명쯤 돼요.
examples.en: The website gets about a thousand visitors a day.
The museum gives visitors a free guidebook.
Visitors, please write your name first.

examples.ko: 가게의 첫 방문자를 큰 소리로 맞이했어요.
examples.en: We greeted the shop's first visitor loudly.
Since you are a visitor, not a customer, parking is free.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 방문자 말고는 들어갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: No one but visitors can enter this building.

explain: 가게에서 물건을 사는 사람은 '손님'이라고 해요. 방문자는 건물, 행사, 홈페이지처럼 어딘가에 찾아온 사람에게 쓰고, '방문객'과 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: A shop customer is a 손님. 방문자 is for someone who comes to a building, an event, or a website, and it can be used much like 방문객.

examples.en: A small rest area was built in the park.
While hiking, I drank water at a rest area.
The elderly gather at the village rest area and chat.

examples.ko: 이 쉼터는 누구나 무료로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Anyone can use this rest area for free.
We looked for a rest area and went into the shade.
The rest area in the middle of the road was clean too.

explain: 공원, 산길, 도로 옆처럼 잠깐 쉬어 가도록 만든 곳에 써요. 건물 안에서 쉬는 공간은 '휴게실'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for places made for a short rest, such as a park, a mountain trail, or the side of a road. A resting space inside a building is called 휴게실.

examples.en: The cat is chasing the mouse.
A mouse is eating the cheese.
In the lab, they do research using mice.
I was startled and hid like a mouse.
The child fed the mouse.
White mice are cute, so they are popular.

explain: '쥐'는 더 넓게 쓰는 말이고, 그중 작은 쥐를 '생쥐'라고 불러요. 실험에 쓰는 쥐를 말할 때도 '생쥐'를 써요.

phrases.example: 비를 맞아서 물에 빠진 생쥐 꼴이에요.
phrases.en: like a mouse that fell in water
phrases.nuance_ko: 비나 물에 흠뻑 젖어서 초라해진 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe someone who is soaking wet and looks bedraggled.

explain_en: 쥐 is the broader word, and the small kind is called 생쥐. The mice used in lab experiments are also called 생쥐.

examples.en: I sprayed hairspray on my hair.
This spray smells nice.
I painted a picture on the wall with spray paint.
There is a mosquito spray in my bag.
The tip of the spray is clogged, so nothing comes out.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 작은 스프레이도 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed a small spray bottle for the trip too.

explain: 분무기처럼 뿜어 나오는 액체 전체에 써요. 머리에 쓰면 '헤어스프레이', 벌레를 쫓으면 '모기 스프레이'처럼 쓰임을 앞에 붙여서 불러요. 뿌릴 때는 '뿌리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It covers any liquid that comes out in a mist. The use goes in front: 헤어스프레이 for hair, 모기 스프레이 for keeping mosquitoes away. To spray it, use 뿌리다.

examples.ko: 그 배우가 카메라를 보고 윙크를 했어요.
examples.en: The actor winked at the camera.
My friend smiled and greeted me with a wink.

examples.ko: 아기가 윙크가 안 돼서 두 눈을 다 감았어요.
examples.en: The baby couldn't wink and closed both eyes.
My face turned red at his wink.

examples.ko: 사진을 찍을 때 윙크도 해 봤어요.
examples.en: I tried winking too when taking the photo.
One wink eased the mood.

explain: '윙크를 하다'가 기본이고 '윙크하다'로 붙여 써도 돼요. 한쪽 눈만 감는 동작이라서, 두 눈을 다 깜빡이는 '눈을 깜빡이다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: The basic form is 윙크를 하다, and 윙크하다 is also fine. It means closing only one eye, so it differs from blinking both eyes (눈을 깜빡이다).

examples.ko: 제 동생은 프로 게이머가 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling wants to become a pro gamer.
Gamers wait for new games to come out.
This chair is popular with gamers.

examples.ko: 저도 게이머라서 게임 소식을 자주 봐요.
examples.en: I'm a gamer too, so I often check game news.
I met a famous gamer in person.

examples.ko: 우리 반에는 게이머 친구가 세 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are three gamer friends in our class.

explain: 게임을 직업으로 하는 사람은 '프로 게이머'라고 해요. 취미로 즐기는 사람은 그냥 '게이머'라고 해요.
explain_en: Someone who plays games as a job is a 프로 게이머. Someone who plays for fun is simply a 게이머.

examples.en: A school anniversary ceremony was held at the school.
The president also attended the ceremony.
The ceremony took about an hour.
We were busy preparing for the ceremony.
After the ceremony, everyone took photos.
The ceremony was cancelled too because of the rain.

explain: '-식'은 행사를 뜻해서 졸업식, 입학식, 결혼식처럼 여러 말에 붙어요. 기념식은 '열리다', '참석하다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: The ending -식 means a ceremony, as in 졸업식, 입학식, and 결혼식. 기념식 is used with verbs like 열리다 and 참석하다.

examples.en: I shave in front of the mirror every morning.
Yesterday I had no time, so I shaved in a rush.

examples.ko: 내일 면접이 있어서 일찍 면도할 거예요.
examples.en: I have an interview tomorrow, so I'll shave early.
My face stung while I was shaving.
I shaved and then put on lotion.
You look clean-faced because you shaved.

explain: '면도기', '면도날', '면도크림'처럼 도구 이름에도 '면도'가 들어가요. 수염과 얼굴 털을 밀 때 쓰고, 머리카락을 짧게 자를 때는 '자르다', '깎다'를 써요.
explain_en: The word 면도 also appears in tool names like 면도기, 면도날, and 면도크림. It is used for shaving a beard or facial hair, while cutting hair short uses 자르다 or 깎다.

examples.en: I lost the car cover.
The cover was blown away by the wind.

examples.ko: 비가 오니까 덮개로 자전거를 덮어 두세요.
examples.en: It's raining, so put a cover over your bike.

examples.ko: 이 덮개는 세탁기에 빨 수 있어요.
examples.en: This cover can be washed in the washing machine.
If you leave it without a cover, dust builds up.
I need to buy a new chair cover too.

explain: '덮다'에서 나온 말이라서 위에 얹어 가리는 물건에 써요. 냄비나 병을 막는 둥근 것은 보통 '뚜껑'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It comes from the verb 덮다 and is used for something laid over a thing to cover it. The round piece that closes a pot or bottle is usually called 뚜껑.

examples.en: In college I joined a photography club.
Our club meets every Friday.
I married a friend I met in the club.
A new club started at the school.
I'm thinking about which club to choose.
The film club is accepting new members too.

explain: 같은 취미로 모인 학생이나 젊은 사람들의 모임을 가리켜요. 요즘은 학교 모임을 '동아리', 취미 모임을 '동호회'라고 더 많이 말해서 '서클'은 조금 옛날 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a group of students or young people gathered around a shared hobby. Today people more often say 동아리 for a school group and 동호회 for a hobby group, so 서클 feels a bit dated.

examples.en: In Busan, I stay at a hotel near the sea.

examples.ko: 지난주에는 친구 집이 아니라 호텔에서 숙박했어요.
examples.en: Last week I stayed at a hotel, not at a friend's house.
This weekend I will stay overnight on Jeju Island.

examples.ko: 숙박하는 사람은 먼저 이름을 적어야 해요.
examples.en: Guests who stay overnight must write their name first.
I stayed one night and left in the morning.
If you want to stay, you have to book in advance.

explain: 호텔이나 펜션처럼 돈을 내고 자는 곳에서 하룻밤 이상 머무는 일에 써요. 말할 때는 '묵다'를 더 자주 써서 '호텔에서 묵다'라고 해요. 친구 집에서 자는 것은 '숙박하다'가 아니라 '자다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for staying one night or more at a paid place like a hotel or pension. In speech, 묵다 is more common, as in 호텔에서 묵다. Sleeping at a friend's house is 자다, not 숙박하다.

examples.en: The apartment security guard said hello.
I left the parcel with the security guard.

examples.ko: 밤에는 경비원 두 명이 건물을 지켜요.
examples.en: At night, two guards watch over the building.
The guard came to work early in the morning.

examples.ko: 저는 경비원을 불러서 문을 열어 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I called the guard and asked him to open the door.
The bank's guard is kind to customers too.

explain: 아파트에서는 친근하게 '경비 아저씨'라고도 불러요. '-원'은 일하는 사람을 뜻해서 은행원, 회사원, 공무원처럼 다른 직업 이름에도 붙어요.
explain_en: In apartment buildings, people also call them 경비 아저씨 in a friendly way. The ending -원 means a worker, and it appears in job names such as 은행원, 회사원, and 공무원.

examples.en: For my health, I'm quitting smoking from this year.
My father quit smoking after visiting the hospital.
I will definitely quit smoking next year.

examples.ko: 금연하는 사람이 요즘 많이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are quitting smoking these days.

examples.ko: 한 달 동안 금연하고 운동도 시작했어요.
examples.en: I quit smoking for a month and started exercising too.
My cough got better because I quit smoking.

explain: 스스로 담배를 끊을 때 '금연하다'를 쓰고, 말할 때는 '담배를 끊다'도 많이 써요. 장소의 규칙은 '금연 구역'처럼 명사로 말하고, 반대말은 '흡연하다'예요.
explain_en: Use 금연하다 when you yourself give up smoking; in speech 담배를 끊다 is also very common. A place's rule is said as a noun, like 금연 구역, and the opposite verb is 흡연하다.

examples.en: A small diamond is set in the ring.
That diamond is very expensive.
He gave his wife a diamond ring.
It's hard to tell a fake diamond apart.
I saw a necklace made of diamonds.
This watch has diamonds in it too.

explain: '다이아몬드'를 줄인 말이라서 대화에서 편하게 써요. 카드 게임에서 ◆ 모양의 카드도 '다이아'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of 다이아몬드, so it is handy in casual talk. The ◆ suit in card games is also called 다이아.

examples.en: You can see many stars in the night sky.
The night sky is prettier in the countryside than in the city.
I made a wish while looking at the night sky.
The dark night sky suddenly lit up.

examples.ko: 캠핑장에서 본 밤하늘도 잊을 수 없어요.
examples.en: I can't forget the night sky I saw at the campsite either.
I went up the mountain to take photos of the night sky.

explain: '밤'과 '하늘'이 붙어서 한 단어가 됐어요. 별, 달과 함께 '별이 가득한 밤하늘'처럼 쓰고, 낮에는 따로 부르지 않고 그냥 '하늘'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It joins 밤 and 하늘 into one word. It goes with stars and the moon, as in 별이 가득한 밤하늘, while the daytime sky is just called 하늘.

examples.en: In science class we looked at cells through a microscope.
The microscope was too expensive, so I borrowed one from school.
They installed a new microscope in the lab.

examples.ko: 이 현미경은 작은 벌레도 크게 보여요.
examples.en: This microscope makes even tiny bugs look big.
A drop of water moved under the microscope.
The institute has an electron microscope too.

explain: '-경'은 렌즈로 보는 도구에 붙어서 안경, 망원경, 현미경처럼 써요. 도구를 나타내는 '으로'와 함께 '현미경으로 보다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: The ending -경 attaches to tools you see through with lenses, as in 안경, 망원경, and 현미경. You say 현미경으로 보다, using the particle 으로 for the tool.

examples.en: I laminate the paper so it won't tear.
Yesterday I laminated my student ID.
I will laminate this poster tomorrow.
Laminating takes about five minutes.
I laminated the photo and stuck it on the wall.

examples.ko: 비에 젖지 않도록 코팅해서 쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: I coat it so it doesn't get wet in the rain, and I use it.

explain: 종이를 비닐로 싸는 일에도, 프라이팬이나 안경 렌즈 겉에 막을 입히는 일에도 써요. 이미 처리된 물건은 '코팅된 종이'처럼 '코팅되다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It is used both for sealing paper in plastic and for putting a layer on the surface of a frying pan or eyeglass lens. A finished item is described with 코팅되다, as in 코팅된 종이.

examples.en: This team's mascot is a tiger.
The mascot danced in the stadium.
The children took photos with the mascot.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 마스코트를 새로 만들고 있어요.
examples.en: We are creating a new mascot for our school.
I attached a small mascot doll to my bag.
The Olympic mascot will be announced soon too.

explain: 팀, 학교, 행사를 대표하는 캐릭터예요. 동물 모양이 많고, '마스코트 인형'처럼 물건으로도 만들어 팔아요.
explain_en: It is the character that represents a team, school, or event. Many are animals, and they are also made into goods, like a 마스코트 인형.

examples.en: Conan is a great detective in a comic.
I want to solve problems like a great detective, too.
The great detective found the culprit right away.
As a child I dreamed of becoming a great detective.
The great detective in that novel wears glasses.

examples.ko: 명탐정 셜록 홈스를 좋아하는 친구가 있어요.
examples.en: I have a friend who likes the great detective Sherlock Holmes.

explain: '명-'은 뛰어나다는 뜻이라서 명배우, 명장면, 명곡처럼 여러 말에 붙어요. 추리를 잘하는 친구에게 농담으로 '명탐정이네'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: The prefix 명- means outstanding and attaches to many words like 명배우, 명장면, and 명곡. People also joke 명탐정이네 to a friend who is good at figuring things out.

examples.en: The children are wrestling in the playground.
Yesterday I wrestled with my uncle.
We will wrestle with family during the holiday.
The wrestlers are standing on the sand ring.

examples.ko: 우리는 한참 씨름하고 나서 땀을 닦았어요.
examples.en: After wrestling for a good while, we wiped off our sweat.
My arm hurts because I wrestled with my brother.

explain: 한국 전통 운동 '씨름'에서 나온 말이에요. 명사 '씨름'은 '씨름을 하다'와 '씨름하다' 두 가지로 모두 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 어제 하루 종일 숙제와 씨름했어요.
phrases.en: struggle with something for a long time
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵거나 잘 풀리지 않는 일을 오래 붙잡고 애쓸 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you keep working at something hard that won't come together.

explain_en: It comes from the traditional Korean sport 씨름. The noun can be used either as 씨름을 하다 or joined as 씨름하다.

examples.en: Ugh, I'm so tired again today.
Oh dear, it's raining again.
Phew, I got such a fright.
Phew, it's finally over.
Ugh! Why is the room so hot?
Oh, please stop it already.

explain: 힘들 때, 안심할 때, 어이없을 때 모두 나오는 소리라서 표정과 억양으로 느낌이 달라져요. 비슷한 소리로 '아이고'가 있어요.
explain_en: It comes out when you are tired, relieved, or exasperated, so the feeling depends on your face and intonation. A similar sound is 아이고.

en: be deposited; be put into a bank account

examples.en: Half of my salary is automatically put into my savings account.

examples.ko: 아껴 둔 돈이 어제 통장에 예금됐어요.
examples.en: The money I saved up was put into my account yesterday.
The New Year gift money will be put into the child's account.

examples.ko: 통장에 예금되는 돈이 조금씩 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: The amount being deposited into my account is slowly growing.
After the money was deposited, a text message came.
A lump sum has been put into my account, so I feel at ease.

explain: 사람이 돈을 은행에 맡기면 '예금하다', 그 돈이 통장에 들어가 쌓이면 '예금되다'로 말해요. 돈이 들어온 것만 말할 때는 '입금되다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: When a person leaves money at a bank, it is 예금하다, and when that money goes into the account and builds up, it is 예금되다. If you only mean that money arrived, 입금되다 is more natural.

examples.en: My friend is a famous pianist.
The pianist came up on stage.
I have dreamed of being a pianist since I was young.
The pianist's hands were really fast.
That pianist performs in Korea every year.
Many young pianists gathered too.

explain: 직업으로 연주하는 사람에게 주로 써요. 취미로 치는 친구는 '피아노를 쳐요'라고 말해요. 바이올린 연주자는 '바이올리니스트'예요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for someone who plays professionally. A friend who plays for fun is described as 피아노를 쳐요. A violin player is a 바이올리니스트.

examples.ko: 식탁 위에 글라스 두 개를 놓았어요.
examples.en: I put two glasses on the table.
I filled the glass with juice.
This glass is thin, so you need to be careful.
The glass fell on the floor and broke.
I served cold water to the guest in a glass.
I bought a few new glasses too.

explain: 물을 마시는 컵은 보통 '컵'이나 '유리컵'이라고 해요. '글라스'는 '선글라스'처럼 다른 말 뒤에 붙을 때가 많아요.
explain_en: A cup for drinking water is usually called 컵 or 유리컵. 글라스 often appears attached to the end of another word, as in 선글라스.

examples.en: The game ended in a tie.
When the score was tied, the crowd shouted.
Our team tied the score at the end.
The two people who were tied competed again.

examples.ko: 시험에서 두 학생이 동점이라 함께 일 등이 됐어요.
examples.en: Two students had the same score on the exam, so they tied for first place.
The equalizing goal came in the second half.

explain: 경기 중에 점수가 같아지는 순간과 점수가 같은 상태에 모두 써요. 경기가 같은 점수로 끝나면 '무승부'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used both for the moment the score becomes level and for the state of being level. A match that ends with equal scores is called a 무승부.

examples.en: I commute by subway.
I used to commute by bus.
From next month I will commute by bike.
My commuting time is too long.

examples.ko: 회사 근처로 이사해서 걸어서 출퇴근하고 있어요.
examples.en: I moved near my office, so I now commute on foot.
My home is close, so I don't get tired even when I commute.

explain: 가는 것은 '출근하다', 돌아오는 것은 '퇴근하다'이고, 둘을 합쳐 말할 때 '출퇴근하다'를 써요. '출퇴근 시간', '출퇴근길'처럼 다른 말과도 붙어요.
explain_en: Going to work is 출근하다 and leaving work is 퇴근하다, and 출퇴근하다 combines the two. It also joins other words, as in 출퇴근 시간 and 출퇴근길.

examples.en: My uncle is a producer at a broadcasting station.
The producer chose the filming location.
I am a college student who dreams of becoming a producer.
The producer manages the program from start to finish.

examples.ko: 그 예능 피디와 인터뷰할 기회가 있었어요.
examples.en: I had a chance to interview that variety show producer.
The producer of this drama came to the set too.

explain: 방송에서 프로그램 제작을 맡은 사람을 가리키고, 'PD'라고 영어로 쓰기도 해요. 앞에 '예능', '드라마'를 붙여 어떤 프로그램인지 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the person in charge of making a broadcast program, and it is also written in English as PD. Put 예능 or 드라마 before it to say which kind of program.

examples.ko: 시험 볼 때 샤프를 가져가야 해요.
examples.en: You need to bring a mechanical pencil when taking the test.
The lead of my mechanical pencil keeps breaking.
A mechanical pencil is more convenient than a pencil.
I take notes with a mechanical pencil.
There is only one mechanical pencil on the desk.
I bought a mechanical pencil at the stationery shop too.

explain: '샤프'는 '샤프펜슬'을 줄인 말이에요. 안에 넣는 가는 심은 '샤프심'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: 샤프 is short for 샤프펜슬. The thin lead that goes inside is called 샤프심.

examples.en: The pitcher threw a strike with the first pitch.

examples.ko: 스트라이크가 세 번 나오면 타자는 아웃이에요.
examples.en: When there are three strikes, the batter is out.

examples.ko: 오늘 볼링에서 연속으로 스트라이크 세 번을 쳤어요.
examples.en: Today in bowling I bowled three strikes in a row.
The umpire saw the ball and called a strike.
The last pitch was ruled a strike.
I hope it's a strike this time too.

explain: 야구에서는 심판이 스트라이크를 선언하고, 반대되는 말은 '볼'이에요. 볼링에서는 첫 공으로 핀을 모두 쓰러뜨릴 때 써요.
explain_en: In baseball the umpire calls a strike, and its opposite is a 볼. In bowling it is used when you knock down all the pins with the first ball.

examples.en: I saw a unicorn in a storybook.
A unicorn has one horn on its forehead.
The child slept holding a unicorn doll.
A white unicorn flew through the sky.
The atmosphere was mysterious, like a unicorn.
A unicorn is drawn on this bag too.

explain: '용'이나 '봉황'처럼 실제로는 없는 상상 속 동물이에요. 사업 이야기에서는 비유로도 써서 '유니콘 기업'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 곧 유니콘 기업이 될 거예요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짧은 기간에 아주 크게 성장한 새 회사를 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a young company that has grown very large in a short time.

explain_en: Like 용 and 봉황, it is an imaginary animal that does not really exist. In business talk it is also used as a metaphor in the phrase 유니콘 기업.

examples.en: I lightly applied powder to my face.
This powder smells nice.
I ran out of powder, so I need to buy more.
I prevented heat rash with baby powder.
I always use powder when I put on makeup.
I took a powder puff out in the restroom.

explain: 화장품에서는 얼굴에 바르는 가루를 말해요. 음식 재료는 '가루'라고 하지만, '단백질 파우더'처럼 외래어 이름에는 '파우더'를 그대로 써요.
explain_en: In cosmetics it means the loose powder you put on your face. Food ingredients are usually called 가루, but loanword names like 단백질 파우더 keep 파우더.

examples.en: My grandfather was diagnosed with lung cancer.
Lung cancer is easier to treat if found early.
The doctor said it was not lung cancer.

examples.ko: 폐암을 예방하려면 검진을 받는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: To prevent lung cancer, it's good to get screened.
My neighbor who suffered from lung cancer recovered.
Lung cancer can also be found in a health checkup.

explain: '폐'는 몸속 장기 이름이고 '암'은 병 이름이에요. '위암', '간암'처럼 장기 이름 뒤에 '암'을 붙여서 '폐암 환자', '폐암 검사'라고 써요.
explain_en: 폐 is the lung and 암 is cancer. Like 위암 and 간암, you attach 암 after the organ name, as in 폐암 환자 or 폐암 검사.

examples.en: My grandmother is a stylish person.

examples.ko: 그 멋쟁이 아저씨를 동네에서 다 알아요.
examples.en: Everyone in the neighborhood knows that stylish man.

examples.ko: 멋쟁이가 되려면 옷을 잘 맞춰 입어야 해요.
examples.en: To be stylish, you have to coordinate your clothes well.
You came out dressed up like a stylish person today.
My friend is stylish, so she works at a clothing shop.
Many stylish people gathered on the street.

explain: '-쟁이'는 어떤 특징이 있는 사람에게 붙는 말로 '욕심쟁이', '개구쟁이'도 있어요. 멋쟁이는 칭찬으로 써서 옷차림이 세련된 사람에게 말해요.
explain_en: The ending -쟁이 attaches to a person with a certain trait, as in 욕심쟁이 and 개구쟁이. 멋쟁이 is a compliment for someone whose clothing looks refined.

examples.en: I sprinkled baking soda when cleaning.
We ran out of baking soda, so I went to the mart.

examples.ko: 이 소다는 설거지에도 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: This baking soda can be used for washing dishes too.
I added a spoonful of baking soda to the dough.
I scrubbed the cup with baking soda and it came out clean.
This snack has baking soda in it too.

explain: 요리와 청소에 쓰는 하얀 가루를 가리킬 때 써요. 더 정확히 말할 때는 '베이킹소다'라고 하고, 거품이 나는 물은 '소다수'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the white powder used in cooking and cleaning. To be more exact, say 베이킹소다, and fizzy water is called 소다수.

examples.en: The teacher handed out printouts.
One printout is missing.
This handout will be on tomorrow's test.
Write your name on the printout and hand it in.
I find it easier to study with printouts.
I put the class handouts in my bag too.

explain: 종이에 인쇄한 수업 자료를 가리킬 때 써요. 옷에 그려진 무늬도 '프린트 티셔츠'처럼 같은 말을 써요. 인쇄하는 일은 '인쇄'나 '프린트하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to course material printed on paper. A pattern on clothes uses the same word, as in 프린트 티셔츠. The act of printing is 인쇄 or 프린트하다.

examples.ko: 이 문서는 하루에 백 장씩 프린트돼요.
examples.en: This document is printed a hundred copies a day.
The test papers have already been printed.
The ticket will be printed soon.
Please wait a moment while it is printing.
After the photo was printed, I put it in a frame.
The letters are printed small, so they are hard to read.

explain: '프린트하다'는 사람이 인쇄하는 쪽이고 '프린트되다'는 종이에 인쇄되어 나오는 쪽을 봐요. '프린트가 나오다'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: 프린트하다 looks at the person who prints, while 프린트되다 looks at what comes out printed on the paper. People also say 프린트가 나오다.

examples.en: There are many small cafes along the coast.
If you walk along the coast, the breeze is cool.
The seaside is crowded in summer.
We picked up shells on the seashore.
Many houses on the coast have blue roofs.
The seaside gets quiet too once the sun sets.

explain: '해안'은 바다와 땅이 만나는 곳이고, '-가'를 붙이면 그 근처를 가리켜요. '강가', '길가'도 같은 방식이고 '바닷가'와 거의 같아요.
explain_en: 해안 is where sea meets land, and adding -가 gives the area near it. 강가 and 길가 are formed the same way, and 해안가 is nearly the same as 바닷가.

examples.en: I caught a crucian carp in the pond.
A crucian carp jumped above the water.
This crucian carp is as big as a palm.
The children fed the crucian carp.

examples.ko: 붕어로 만든 찜이 유명한 식당에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to a restaurant famous for braised crucian carp.
They sell crucian carp at the market too.

explain: 붕어 모양 간식 '붕어빵'에는 붕어가 들어가지 않아요. 연못이나 강에 사는 민물고기라서 낚시나 매운탕 이야기에도 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 가족끼리 얼굴이 똑같이 닮았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when family members look exactly alike.

explain_en: The fish-shaped snack 붕어빵 contains no 붕어. It is a freshwater fish of ponds and rivers, so it comes up in talk about fishing and 매운탕.

examples.en: The bus goes around a curve up ahead.
The curve was sharp, so I drove slowly.
This road has a long curved section.
The pitcher fooled the batter with a curveball.
The bike slid on the curve.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 커브도 던질 줄 알아요.
examples.en: That player can throw a curveball too.

explain: 도로의 휘어진 곳에도, 야구에서 휘어서 날아가는 공에도 써요. 도로에서 심하게 굽은 곳은 '급커브'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is used for a bend in a road and for a pitch that bends in baseball. A very sharp bend in a road is called 급커브.

examples.en: Saturn has large rings around it.
I looked at Saturn through a telescope.

examples.ko: 토성에는 아직 사람이 가 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: No human has been to Saturn yet.
Saturn looked bright in the night sky.

examples.ko: 토성의 고리는 얼음과 돌로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: Saturn's rings are made of ice and rock.
Saturn is a very big planet like Jupiter.

explain: 토성의 '토'는 토요일의 '토'(흙)와 같은 글자예요. 목성은 목요일의 '목'(나무)처럼 행성 이름과 요일 이름이 이어져요.
explain_en: The 토 in 토성 is the same character as the 토 (earth) in 토요일. Likewise 목성 shares 목 (wood) with 목요일, so planet names and weekday names are linked.

examples.en: I saw a gorilla at the zoo.
The gorilla beat its chest.
Gorillas eat leaves.
The child walked like a gorilla.
I received a gorilla doll as a gift.
Gorillas also live together in family groups.

explain: '침팬지'와 같은 무리의 동물이에요. 몸은 침팬지보다 훨씬 크고, 꼬리가 없다는 점은 같아요.
explain_en: It belongs to the same group of animals as the 침팬지. A gorilla is much bigger than a chimpanzee, and both have no tail.

examples.en: The weather is warm today.
The tea I drank yesterday was very warm.
Tomorrow will be warmer than now.
I felt energized after eating warm soup.

examples.ko: 방이 따듯하고 조용해서 잠이 잘 와요.
examples.en: The room is warm and quiet, so I fall asleep easily.
The blanket is warm, so I don't want to go outside.

explain: '따뜻하다'와 함께 둘 다 표준어예요. 온도가 알맞게 높을 때 쓰고, 그보다 센 온도는 '뜨겁다'라고 해요. 다정한 사람이나 마음에도 써요.
explain_en: Both 따듯하다 and 따뜻하다 are standard forms. It is for a pleasantly high temperature, while something hotter is 뜨겁다. It also describes a kind person or heart.

examples.en: My account went into the minus.
The temperature dropped to minus five degrees.
This month the business is at a loss.

examples.ko: 급할 때를 위해 마이너스 통장을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I opened an overdraft account for emergencies.
That is not a disadvantage for us.
The calculation came out negative.

explain: 반대말은 '플러스'예요. 숫자 앞에 붙는 '-'뿐 아니라 돈이 모자라는 것, 손해, 도움이 안 되는 일에도 비유로 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 통장에 돈이 없어도 정해진 한도까지 빌려 쓸 수 있는 통장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An account that lets you borrow up to a set limit even with no balance.

explain_en: Its opposite is 플러스. Besides the "-" sign before a number, it is used figuratively for a shortage of money, a loss, or something unhelpful.

examples.en: Oh my goodness, I left my wallet at home.
Good heavens! It's already ten o'clock.
Oh my, good heavens. What is all this?
I cried out, "Good heavens!"
I saw my test score and said, "Oh my goodness."
Oh, good heavens, we're really in trouble.

explain: '세상에', '어머'와 비슷하게 놀랐을 때 해요. 주로 곤란하거나 나쁜 일을 봤을 때 써요.
explain_en: Like 세상에 and 어머, it is said when you are shocked. It mostly goes with troublesome or bad events.
